title: Flameweaver CI collector runbook and smoke scripts
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note captures a compact, reproducible runbook + lightweight scripts used by the perf CI to collect flamegraphs, off-cpu stacks, and short traces for investigating regressions in the serving runtime. The goal is a small, standard artifact that CI can produce in < 10 minutes for typical unit-loads and a slightly longer smoke-run for heavy paths (KV cache hotpath, attention kernel handoffs).

Design goals (constraints):
- minimal agent: shell + python3, no heavy container image changes in CI.
- deterministic collection: fixed sampling frequency, reproducible start/stop hooks.
- small artifact sizes: strip debug extras, keep top-100 stacks.
- capture both user stacks and kernel off-cpu stacks where relevant.
- optional GPU timeline capture (ncu/nsys) triggered by a feature flag.

Quick TL;DR commands (local dev):
1) perf (CPU) flamegraph collection for a running server (gcc/clang builds with frame pointers):
  sudo perf record -F 99 -g -p $(pidof serving-bin) -- sleep 15
  sudo perf script > /tmp/perf.stacks
  ./tools/stackcollapse-perf.pl /tmp/perf.stacks > /tmp/perf.folded
  ./tools/flamegraph.pl /tmp/perf.folded > flame-perf.svg

2) off-cpu stack capture (useful for sched/jitter):
  sudo perf record -e sched:sched_switch -g -p $(pidof serving-bin) -- sleep 10
  sudo perf script -i perf.data > offcpu.stacks

3) Lightweight eBPF sampler (bcc/tbolt mode) for async code paths:
  sudo ./tools/ebpf/sampler.py --pid $(pidof serving-bin) --duration 12 --freq 200 --output ebpf.json

4) GPU capture (NVidia Nsight CLI) -- gated, run only on dedicated jobs:
  nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=host --output gpu-timeline ./run-smoke-client.sh

CI job pattern (narrative):
- job triggers: nightly + PRs that touch runtime/ or CI-detected latency regression.
- step 1: deploy a small dedicated test binary on an ephemeral node (prebuilt release candidate).
- step 2: run a deterministic client: 20 concurrent threads, prompt distribution fixture (short+long mixes). 60s warmup + 30s capture window.
- step 3: run collectors in parallel: perf (cpu), ebpf sampler, optional nsys.
- step 4: archive artifacts (perf.data, folded stacks, flamegraphs, ebpf.json, nsys.qdrep) to artifacts bucket and post a PR comment with links.

Example lightweight CI YAML snippet (annotated):
# (this is pseudo-yaml for readability — real CI config lives in .ci/collectors/)
- name: start smoke server
  run: |
    ./scripts/start-smoke-server.sh --config=ci/fast-24.yaml &
    echo $! > /tmp/serving_pid

- name: perf collect
  run: |
    PID=$(cat /tmp/serving_pid)
    sudo perf record -F 120 -g -p $PID -- sleep 30
    sudo perf script -i perf.data > perf.script
    python3 tools/ci_fold_and_upload.py perf.script perf.folded flame-perf.svg $CI_ARTIFACTS_URL

- name: ebpf sampler (optional)
  if: matrix.collect_ebpf == true
  run: |
    sudo tools/ebpf/sampler.py --pid $PID --duration 30 --freq 250 --output ebpf.json
    curl -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARTIFACT_TOKEN" --data-binary @ebpf.json $CI_ARTIFACTS_URL/ebpf.json

Collector implementation notes:
- Use perf with -F 99 for stable sampling across linux VMs; adjust to 120 for short windows to get better resolution.
- If using frame-pointers (recommended), compile with -fno-omit-frame-pointer. For C++ code with heavy inlining, add -g to preserve symbol names for the flamegraph.
- For builds where we can't change compile flags (third-party libs), enable 'perf map' by generating a /tmp/perf-<pid>.map file mapping native addresses to function names (tools/perf_map_gen.py).
- eBPF sampler is a best-effort path for async stacks (green threads, io uring callbacks). It records user stack + kernel stack and serializes to compressed JSON. The python collector script decodes and collapses to the same folded format used by flamegraph.pl.

Artifact hygiene and size controls:
- Trim flamegraph svg to top 200 frames before storing using svg-prune.py (keeps the svg but reduces bytes).
- Convert perf.data -> perf.script and immediately collapse; do not store raw perf.data unless a follow-up deeper investigation is requested. Keep retention policy: 14 days by default, 90 days for labeled regressions.

Troubleshooting checklist (common failures in CI):
- "perf: failed to record" -> check kernel perf_event_paranoid (CI node should be provisioned with paranoid=1). If higher, use CAP_SYS_ADMIN or run in privileged runner.
- No symbols in flamegraph -> verify build type (release with stripped symbols will show addresses). If necessary, grab unstripped binary from artifacts store or use perf map trick.
- Huge artifact sizes -> reduce sampling duration or use higher frequency + shorter window; prefer folded stacks over raw data.
- eBPF sampler crashes on older kernels -> fallback to perf + short sampling windows. Add kernel-version gating in CI matrix.

Quick diagnosis recipes (one-liners):
- top CPU by function (local): grep -A5 "top-level" flame-perf.svg or open file in browser and inspect wide blocks.
- find off-cpu hotspots: look at offcpu.stacks and search for functions that only appear in off-cpu traces (locking/syscalls).
- correlate GPU stalls: open nsys timeline, filter for cudaMemcpy + kernel launches; if CPU thread is waiting on memcpy, check pinned memory usage.

Example observations we've seen recently (notes):
- "KV cache churn" scenario: large flame block inside kvcache::lookup that disappears when sampling window shortened; indicates heavy contention rather than long-tail latency.
- "Context refill" pattern: repeated small stacks where runtime::enqueue_call dominates on CPU and tens of GPU memcpy ops follow in the timeline — points to serialization in host->device staging.
- "Sampler amplification" bug: eBPF sampler itself added measurable jitter when run at 1kHz across many threads; reduced freq to 200Hz for CI to avoid perturbing the system.

TODOs / follow-ups:
- (Aisha) add perf map generator to the smoke image and instrument CI to upload unstripped binaries to ephemeral bucket on job start.
- (Marco) add kernel-version matrix gating to skip eBPF tests on <=5.10.
- (Elena) prototype a small Rust-based collector that produces smaller compressed folded stacks (RUST-collector branch).

Reference scripts and locations:
- tools/ci_fold_and_upload.py — collapsing + upload helper (repo: serving-runtime/tools/)
- tools/ebpf/sampler.py — bcc-based sampler wrapper
- tools/perf_map_gen.py — generate perf maps for address->symbol mapping
- .ci/collectors/ — CI job templates (live configs)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally compact and pragmatic. It's a working runbook for the oncall/perf triage flow and the CI job templates. Please add missing failure modes you hit when collecting on k8s nodes or on bare-metal.

Changelog:
- 2025-01-15: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2025-01-22: added eBPF fallback notes and artifact retention policy (Marco)
- 2025-02-03: GPU capture gating and TODOs for perf map (Elena)

End of runbook.
